title: Tenali Raman and the Iron Sandal Challenge

full_text:
A gigantic warrior and martial artist named Malakallu arrived at the court of Vijayanagara, wearing heavy armor and carrying an enormous iron club. He had defeated dozens of champions in wrestling and swordplay.
Malakallu slammed a pair of thick iron sandals onto the King’s audience carpet, boasting:
'I challenge the scholars and ministers of Vijayanagara to a duel of endurance!
Whosoever can wear these solid iron sandals, walk across fifty paces of glowing charcoal, and emerge without injury shall be crowned Champion of the Deccan!
If none dare, your Emperor must acknowledge that your courtiers are cowards!'

The court was silent in dismay. Walking across burning charcoal in solid iron sandals would roast a man’s feet to the bone, as iron conducts intense heat instantly!
King Krishnadevaraya looked anxiously at Tenali Raman.

Tenali stepped forward with a serene smile:
'I accept the challenge, Malakallu! But according to ancient codes of honor, since thou didst choose the sandals, I have the right to set the testing conditions!'
Malakallu laughed arrogance: 'Set whatever conditions thou wilt, jester!'

Tenali said: 'Very well! We shall both wear iron sandals and walk across the coals.
However, ancient codes state that champions must face the trial simultaneously, side by side!
Furthermore, to ensure absolute fairness, thy iron sandals shall be tied to thy feet with ropes of pitch-soaked hemp, and my sandals shall be tied to mine!'

Malakallu agreed, boasting: 'I fear nothing!'

The charcoal pit was prepared in the palace courtyard, glowing red-hot with intense heat.
Tenali had the royal blacksmiths strap the heavy iron sandals securely to Malakallu’s feet with pitch-soaked ropes.
Tenali then put on his own pair of iron sandals.

As they stood at the edge of the blazing pit, Tenali turned to the King and proclaimed:
'Maharaj, let the duel begin!
According to the rules of simultaneous trial, the challenger must step onto the coals first to lead the way, and I shall step immediately behind him!'

Malakallu looked at the glowing coals, then looked at his heavy iron sandals strapped to his feet.
He suddenly realized the horrific reality:
The moment his iron sandals touched the glowing coals, the iron would superheat within seconds, the pitch-soaked ropes would catch fire, and his feet would be incinerated before he could take three steps!
He would be roasted alive!

Malakallu’s courage evaporated into sheer panic.
He backed away frantically, screaming:
'No! I yield! Unstrap these sandals! I withdraw the challenge!'

He fell to the floor, sweating and trembling, begging for royal pardon!
The entire court burst into roaring laughter as the boastful giant squirmed to unstrap his own iron shoes!

Tenali smiled, took off his unheated sandals, and said:
'True valor does not consist in creating cruel, destructive trials to humiliate others. A man who lives by the fire of arrogance is always the first to be burned by his own flames!'

The King banished the bully, rewarding Tenali Raman for defending the honor of Vijayanagara without spilling a single drop of blood.
moral: Boastful champions who threaten peaceful courts with violent wagers are disarmed by quick-witted rules of engagement.
